chunks: 3414 - Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:
Regarding His, Mighty and Majestic, saying:
"And Dawud and Sulayman, when they were judging concerning the field, when the sheep of the people strayed into it."
He عليه السلام said: "They did not pass judgment; rather, they were discussing the matter: 'So We gave Sulayman understanding of it.'"

key_terms.الْحَرْثِ: the cultivated field or crop under dispute
key_terms.سُلَيْمَانَ: Sulayman, to whom the understanding in this case was given
key_terms.فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا: So We gave understanding of it
key_terms.نَفَشَتْ: strayed by night and spread into the field
key_terms.يَتَنَاظَرَانِ: they were discussing and examining the matter together
key_terms.يَحْكُمَانِ: they were judging or considering judgment in the case

ai.seo_question: What does the verse about Dawud and Sulayman judging over the field mean?
ai.summary: This narration explains the Qur'anic account of Dawud and Sulayman by clarifying that they were not issuing finalized judgments at that moment, but were examining and discussing the case. It highlights Sulayman's divinely granted understanding in the matter and presents the verse as an example of insight in judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3414 - Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):
Regarding the words of Allah (swt), the Exalted:
"And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field, when the sheep of the people had strayed into it" (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:78).
Imam (as) said: "They did not pass a judgment; rather, they were discussing the matter. 'And We gave Solomon understanding of it" (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:79).
